## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `sketch-backed-affinity-state`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-07T15:57:35.738Z.

(8) Sketch-backed scorer state for million-item scale — (6)'s write-time fold keeps per-item activation and per-author affinity counters, but at the pm-g2zz extreme (millions of items x thousands of concurrent authors) exact per-(author, item/tag) counter matrices become the new scale bottleneck: state grows O(authors x touched-items) and dominates the derived read index. Replace exact counters with probabilistic sketches, each with provable error bounds: (a) Count-Min sketch for author-affinity and tag/field co-occurrence counts (sub-linear memory, point-query overestimate bounded by epsilon*N with tunable width/depth); (b) HyperLogLog for distinct-cardinality signals (how many distinct authors/sessions touched this subtree — a trust/centrality input) at ~1.5KB per counter regardless of cardinality; (c) exponential-decay variants (time-decayed CM sketch) so ACT-R-style recency folding from (1) composes directly — decay applied at fold time, no rescan. Spectrum-neutral by construction: below a size threshold the fold stores EXACT counters and the sketch path is dormant; the switchover is an internal representation change invisible to --explain-ranking consumers (signal semantics identical, only precision epsilon differs, and the envelope can disclose 'approximate' when sketched). Derived-never-authoritative holds: sketches are read-index state, rebuildable from immutable history streams at any time; error compounds only within a rebuild epoch. Composes with (7)'s funnel — per-source top-k slates read sketch summaries, never raw streams — and with (5) RRF, which consumes ranks and is inherently robust to bounded count error. SDK-side behind scoreContextCandidates like (1)-(7).

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.

value.text: Sketch experiment constraints: declare epsilon/delta, counter width, hash family and seed, update model and merge compatibility. A Count-Min point estimate has a stream-mass-relative additive error under its required nonnegative assumptions; that error can swamp a rare but important fact. Author discussion: https://dimacs.rutgers.edu/~graham/pubs/papers/sk.pdf . Compare approximate affinity with exact counters on skewed streams and measure downstream ranking loss. Never use probabilistic counters to establish ownership, policy permission, immutable proof, blocker satisfaction or exact population counts; those remain exact contracts.
